body:
### Purpose

With the next changes are adding a Menu entry in the Group ContextMenu, now it will be showing all the GroupStyles added in the Preferences panel, so if a style is added or removed, the ContextMenu GroupStyle will be updated.
Basically I created one base class named GroupStyle base and two child classes GroupStyleItemEntry and GroupStyleSeparator, those classes will be used to select the right Style depending if is a MenuItem or a Separator.
Also I added several resources to avoid using hard-coded strings.
I modified the AnnotationView for adding an entry in the ContextMenu that will be showing all the GroupStyles, also I added a Style for the MenuItem so it can show the scrolbar when there are several MenuItems.
I added the logic for the GroupStyles context menu, this are the rules:
- If a Custom GroupStyle is selected and the user clicks it then the Default Style will be selected.
- If no GroupStyle is selected and the user clicks a specific GroupStyle then it will be selected and the style will be applied to the Group.
Finally I added two unit tests, one is validating that the Default Styles exists and the other one will be adding a style and checking that is shown in the Group ContextMenu.

author: andrew-boyd
body:
So this is super easy and also more robust than trying to handle things on the FormKit side. 

with this package added to your `package.json` in your tailwind config you do this:

```
module.exports = {
  ...
  plugins: [
    require('@formkit/tailwindcss')
  ],
}
```

And then in your classes using the existing FormKit props / config you can use variants such as `formkit-invalid:border-red-500`. Can also be combined with other modifiers because that logic happens on Tailwind's side `hover:formkit-invalid:border-red-500`.

current variants are:
- `formkit-invalid:`
- `formkit-errors:`
- `formkit-disabled:`
- `formkit-complete:`
- `formkit-multiple:`

With this in mind, a few things would make styling easier:

- On the top level form it would be great if there was a `data-submitted="true` attribute so that we could have a `formit-submitted:` variant in Tailwind
- The `classes` prop in the FormKit config that you can override in `defaultConfig` only has section keys. It would be great if we could have our object be structured by type and then by section key. eg: 
```
config: {
  classes: {
    global: {
      label: '...',
      input: '...',
      ...
    },
    text: {
      label: '...',
      input: '...',
      ...
    }
  }
}
```
With that level of specificity combined with the FormKit plugin for Tailwind it would be possible to write a pretty comprehensive Tailwind theme with a simple POJO and no need to fuss with the `rootClasses` function.

author: vezenovm
body:
Basic original changes to switch from using unified memory for gpu ops. I wanted more control over memory synchronization as well as the ability to add more advanced CUDA features not supported with unified memory.  

Lots of comments and stuff that can be cleaned up still, this was for original testing for future branches to work from.

Originally there was implicit synchronization with the stream ordered memcpy's and kernel execution. This PR is now working asynchronously with the host. The later PRs currently open were based off of broken logic from old work in this PR. They will need to be updated with a merge, or a new PR should be created.

body:
Signed-off-by: Hillary Fraley <hfraley@sumologic.com>

## Description
Hides or does not display the code copy button for response examples.

My thoughts about how to do this:
- Hugo renders content placed inside `{{< code >}}` tags with [Chroma](https://github.com/alecthomas/chroma) for syntax highlighting.
     - If you inspect the HTML, all code examples are inside `<pre>` HTML tags, with a nested `<code>` tag.
     - The `<code>` tag includes a class based on the language specified in the Hugo `{{< code >}}` tags. For example, text inside `{{< code shell >}}` tags is rendered in HTML like `<code class="language-shell" data-lang="shell">`.
- Since all content inside code formatting tags in Hugo is rendered with the language-based class and data-lang attribute, I should be able to target this language-based information by adding some kind of if-else statement in the existing clip.js file.
- If I use `{{< code text >}}` tags for responses, the code formatting will still display properly for things like tables copied from terminal. This will produce the HTML `<code class="language-text" data-lang="text">`.
- I think I can target either the class or the data-lang attribute to use either `button.style.visibility="hidden"` or `button.style.display="none"` to avoid showing the copy button for responses (in other words, the content placed inside `{{< code text >}}` tags).

So far, this has not worked. Maybe the problem is one of these things:
- I need to place the code to remove the button after the button is available in the DOM. I think the latest commit achieves this, but I'm not sure.
- The code to hide the button is working, but it's being applied too broadly. The latest commit shows the copy button on the first code example, but then does not show it on any others. I think this means I am targeting incorrectly or incompletely. Or maybe I need to add something more than the "if" statement for hiding the button -- something that says "this only applies to the current content inside the targeted tags, so run this evaluation again every time you hit a code tag." I can't figure out how to test this.

## Motivation and Context
Closes https://github.com/sensu/sensu-docs/issues/3003

This is a major python update cycle that we do every once in a while. The last major update cycle started around mid-january (https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/154969).

- Updates of `hypothesis` can be fragile for a huge number of package tests
  - 6.39.0 caused issues with pytest-asyncio, downgraded to 6.38.0
- `slackclient` before version 3.0, after that it's called `slack-sdk`, they're two distinct packages

Evaluations will appear shortly over at https://hydra.nixos.org/jobset/nixpkgs/python-updates.

The previous cycle can be found in #160067.

body: # Description Panels are a new UI element similar to the already existing Drawer. Panels were designed to with with the panels vue plugin which is also part of this PR. The goal of this PR was to not only make panels look and function correctly but to make using them easy. [Panel Design from Figma](https://www.figma.com/file/JomY9jsgJdal9wfPBtpWkY/UI?node-id=3538%3A133525) ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6200442/156453219-da1a9a54-92d5-4eba-b2ec-dc2b659117a3.png) ## Example By installing miter the `Panel` plugin is also installed. To show a panel first create a panel component. A panel component should use the `m-panel` component as its layout. Using the slots and slot scopes from `m-panel` you can do things like add a title, content, and actions. You can also use the `close` and `exit` methods which are scoped to each slot. ``` ``` Then from the component where you would like to trigger your panel to be shown import the `showPanel` method from miter design. Then you can trigger your panel to be shown by calling that method and passing in your panel component and any props that might be required. ``` import { showPanel } from '@prefecthq/miter-design` import { FlowPanel } from '@/components/flowPanel.vue` showPanel(FlowPanel, { flow: ... }) ``` The `FlowPanel` component will be shown with the props provided. And additional calls of `showPanel` will open another panel on top of any panels that are already open. Closing a panel will reveal the previously opened panel if there is one or it will close and reveal the page it was opened from.
